speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the distinctions between social carpooling and illegal carpooling as defined by the Ministry; and (b) what action will the Ministry take to stop the use of chat groups that facilitate illegal carpooling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Details of booked trips are also recorded by operators, which can be used to aid investigations in the event of an incident or a dispute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We would urge members of the public to book their journeys only with carpooling operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Commuters who encounter such drivers can also file a report with LTA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will social carpooling individuals be put in a difficult situation if LTA tightens regulations towards illegal carpooling and how effective is LTA's enforcement in differentiating between the two practices?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, as many carpooling groups can operate through chatgroups, such as Telegram, how does the Ministry of Transport (MOT) intend to leverage technology and work with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) to monitor such groups?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the past, we have had reports of disputes as well as assault cases arising from unregulated carpooling services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But social carpooling arrangements – generally made between friends or colleagues, typically with no payment made – are permitted.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And usually, this is taken either through public feedback or if LTA conducts enforcement operations that are targeted at these illegal carpooling activities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA will exercise reasonableness and will not intervene if they are purely social carpooling arrangements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is only not allowed if the driver does not have a valid vocational licence and does not drive a private hire car; then, that would be illegal.
